indication.label: Indication (FDA-labeled diagnosis)
indication.hint: Closed list from Alaska Medicaid Ebglyss criteria, effective 2026-03-01; topical prescription therapies inadequately control disease or are not advisable. Weight ≥40 kg is attestation-only in notes, not a predicate.

prescriber_specialty.label: Prescriber or consulting specialist
prescriber_specialty.hint: Must be prescribed by or in consultation with an allergist, immunologist, or dermatologist.

ad_bsa_severity_documented.label: AD: baseline BSA affected and symptom severity documented

ad_topical_failures.label: AD: tried/failed or contraindication (≥2 for 30 days)
ad_topical_failures.hint: Select therapies tried and failed for at least 30 days or contraindicated. At least two of TCS / TCI / PDE4 are required. The remaining-agents contraindication option attests to a distinct remaining class; do not double-count a selected class. The PDF does not specify TCS potency at exactly age 18.

not_used_with_another_biologic.label: Not used with another biologic (e.g. Adbry, Dupixent, Xolair)

criteria.text: Diagnosis is moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, inadequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable.
Patient meets FDA-labeled age for Ebglyss: at least 12 years.
Prescribed by or in consultation with an allergist, immunologist, or dermatologist.

Baseline affected BSA AND symptom severity documented; tried and failed for 30 days or contraindication to at least two of: TCS (medium–high potency if >18 years / low potency if <18 years), topical calcineurin inhibitor, PDE4 inhibitor.
Denial if used in conjunction with another biologic medication (e.g. Adbry, Dupixent, Xolair).

max_units.notes: Month 1: up to six 250 mg injections; Months 2–4: up to two 250 mg injections each month; Month 5 and later: one 250 mg injection monthly. Initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months. Quantity limits are attestation-only, not numeric predicates.

notes: Partial encoding from AK Ebglyss (lebrikizumab-lbkz), an IL-13 antagonist, Criteria Version 1 (Original 12/22/2025, Accepted 01/16/2026, Effective 03/01/2026).

Encoded: closed moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis indication; FDA age ≥12 years; specialty or consultation; baseline affected BSA and symptom severity documentation; at least two topical classes tried/failed for 30 days or contraindicated; no concomitant biologic. Failure to meet approval criteria results in denial.

Weight ≥40 kg appears in the FDA indication text, not as a separate numbered approval criterion; criterion 1 specifies FDA labeling approved age. Weight is attestation-only in notes, not predicated or collected as a fact. A predicate pass does not verify weight eligibility.

Attestation only, not numeric predicates: BSA percentage, symptom severity, topical potency and 30-day trial duration, contraindications, and monthly quantity math. TCS wording follows the PDF (>18 years medium–high potency; <18 years low potency); exactly age 18 is unspecified. Shared Adbry and Dupixent AD option values are retained.
Duration notes only: initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months. The PDF specifies no additional reauthorization response predicate.

Cautions, not approval gates: monitor for hypersensitivity and new or worsening eye symptoms; avoid live vaccines; treat pre-existing helminth infections before initiation, and discontinue Ebglyss until infection resolves if an infection during treatment fails to respond to anti-helminth treatment.
Alternatives: Adbry and Dupixent are evaluate()-linked preferred peers for overlapping atopic dermatitis. Ebglyss is PDL non-preferred in IMMUNOMODULATORS, ATOPIC DERMATITIS.
